title: The Credential and the Skill
sentences: Education has quietly separated into two enterprises that merely happen to share a building.
One of them teaches and the other certifies, and only the second is genuinely priced.
Employers rarely inspect what was actually learned, because inspection is slow and expensive.
They read the certificate instead, which is cheap, immediate and roughly indicative of ability.
The arrangement holds only for as long as the two things remain loosely correlated.
Almost every incentive inside the system works steadily to loosen that correlation further.
Students optimise for the signal rather than the skill, as any rational person would do.
Institutions competing for those same students learn to supply the signal generously.
The result is not fraud so much as a slow and largely unremarked drift of purpose.
What ends up being sold is admission to a category rather than any demonstrable competence.
